title: Rhombohedral Graphene: A Tale of Many Crystals
authors: Ahmed Abouelkomsan, Filippo Gaggioli, Daniele Guerci, Liang Fu
abstract: Experiments on rhombohedral graphene have uncovered an extraordinary wealth of correlated quantum phases - from chiral superconductors to electronic crystals - all within a single family of atomically thin materials. Here, we introduce a simple indicator, derived from the noninteracting band dispersion, that identifies strongly correlated regions in the phase diagram of rhombohedral graphene as a function of carrier density and displacement field. We develop a neural-network variational Monte Carlo method, combined with Hartree-Fock theory, to solve the interacting ground states. Our calculation reveals a variety of electron crystals with no classical analog. These include, at increasing density: Wigner crystal, self-doped Wiger crystal, as well as ''anticrystal'', a lattice of holes in an electron liquid. We discuss their experimental manifestations and possible connection to superconductivity.
summary: This paper investigates the complex quantum phase diagram of rhombohedral graphene, revealing multiple correlated electronic phases. Using advanced computational methods like NN-VMC, the authors predict novel crystalline structures, such as 'anticrystals,' that arise from strong electron-electron interactions tuned by external fields. This work advances our understanding of emergent order in low-dimensional correlated materials.
main_problem: The study aims to identify the organizing principles governing the emergence, competition, and coexistence of strongly correlated quantum phases in rhombohedral graphene.
main_result: The authors predict unconventional quantum crystals, including a self-doped crystal and an 'anticrystal' (a lattice of holes), which are not found in classical systems.
method: They employ a combination of Neural-Network Variational Monte Carlo (NN-VMC) methods with Hartree-Fock theory to solve for the interacting ground states.
model_or_system: The system is rhombohedral graphene, an atomically thin carbon multilayer whose low-energy band structure can be tuned by carrier density ($n$) and a displacement field ($D$).
key_observables: Charge density profiles, the ratio $	ext{reff} = E_{	ext{int}} / E_{	ext{kin}}$, and the charge gap ($\Delta_{HF}$).
important_parameters: Carrier density ($n$), displacement field ($D$), and the indicator value $	ext{reff}$ (strong correlation occurs when $	ext{reff} \ge 20$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations like neglecting certain derivative terms in momentum space calculations, particularly in the thin-annulus limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate band structure changes (single vs. annular Fermi sea) and show ground-state charge densities for four distinct crystalline states discovered via NN-VMC.
paper_structure: The paper systematically maps out the energy landscape by varying $D$ and $n$, using $	ext{reff}$ as a guide to predict transitions between various correlated phases, including Wigner crystals and anti-crystals.
why_interesting: The work provides detailed theoretical predictions for exotic insulating and superconducting states in 2D materials, offering concrete targets for experimental verification relevant to strongly interacting electron systems.
